question:
A plane passes through the point $P(1,-2,3)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$.
(i) Obtain its vector equation.
(ii) Hence obtain its Cartesian equation.
explanation:
Step 1: Position and normal vectors
The position vector of $P(1,-2,3)$ is
$$\vec{a}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k},$$
and a normal vector to the plane is
$$\vec{N}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}.$$
Step 2: Point-normal form of the plane
A plane through a point with position vector $\vec{a}$ and perpendicular to $\vec{N}$ satisfies
$$\vec{N}\cdot(\vec{r}-\vec{a})=0.$$
Step 3: Vector equation
Since $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{N}=2-2-6=-6$, the vector equation becomes
$$\vec{r}\cdot(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})=-6.$$
Step 4: Cartesian conversion
Putting $\vec{r}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}$ gives
$$2x+y-2z=-6.$$
Step 5: Final result
Thus, the vector equation is $\vec{r}\cdot(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})=-6$, and the Cartesian equation is
$$2x+y-2z+6=0.$$
